_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Metroid (USA) (ADR-0239: coverage past the
first stage comes from a selector swept per game and is measured as a
union). Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py; the entry scripts it
names are written by scripts/stages/metroid/password-entry.py.
RUNG 1, NOT RUNG 2. ADR-0239 s1 says to use the first rung that reaches
the place, and for Metroid that is rung 1: the game's own selector, by
input. navigation.kind is 'input', so no cheat rides with any session and
every session is an ADR-0184 s2 'clean' pass that all four surfaces may
read. A password is named in s1's first rung explicitly - 'a menu, a
track or round choice, a password, a continue code'.
Rung 2 was available and is deliberately not used. DataCrystal's Metroid RAM
map publishes '$0074 Current level ($10 = Brinstar, $11 = Norfair, $12 = Kraid,
$13 = Tourian, $14 = Ridley)', the address is below 0x0800, and the rung-1
selector reaches every area, so ADR-0239 s1's ladder stops at rung 1. Pinning
$0074 would buy nothing and cost something: a pin substitutes the byte on the
CPU read bus (ADR-0184 s1), and ADR-0239 s4 warns that a byte read back through
one is either the pin or a value the game stored after reading it.
$0074 is READ here, though, and it is the check. Nothing is pinned anywhere in
this profile, so what each value asserts is a byte the game itself wrote - and
which byte that is is decided by the password, not by the table (see THE RAM
CHECK below). The vendored cheat database is no help to rung 2 either: it ships
exactly two RAM codes for this ROM (UI/Dependencies/Internal/CheatDb.Nes.json,
sha1 FDBFC7871962F72A1EF57E5A7E456164FB93430B, 'Have all items' 6878:FF and
'Infinite energy, Missiles and all items' 69B2:01), both WRAM, which ADR-0184
s1 refuses by address; every other code it lists for this ROM is a letter code
- a PRG patch by construction.
THE SELECTOR. Read off this ROM's own screens on 2026-09-26
(headless_record probe sessions under runs/f1417/metroid/probe/, each
save-state read with scripts/mss_ram.py; the screenshots are kept beside
them):
title screen   'METROID / PUSH START BUTTON / (c) 1986 NINTENDO'. Engine
mode $1D = 1 (DataCrystal's
'Engine mode (0 = game, 1 = title/password)'). DataCrystal's
'Title mode' byte $1F is NOT used here: measured over the first twenty seconds from power-on it counts 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 0D, so it moves with the screen's animation and identifies no screen.
option screen  Start opens 'START / CONTINUE'. Select is the key that
moves the crosshair between the two ($0325, DataCrystal's
'Title/Password Cursor' block: 0 = START selected, 1 =
PASSWORD selected); the D-pad, A and B do nothing here,
measured one run per button with $0325 unmoved in each.
Start confirms and the password screen follows.
password       'PASS WORD PLEASE' over a keyboard of five rows of
thirteen columns: the 64 characters that fit in six bits
each, 24 of them per password (24 x 6 = 144 = the 128-bit
payload plus the shift byte plus the checksum, the
encoding the Metroid Password Format Guide documents).
The alphabet in reading order is 0-9, A-Z, a-z, '?' and
'-' - and the keyboard is five rows of thirteen cells, so the

cursor has 65 places to sit: cell (4,12), the one the last row does not draw a glyph on, types the alphabet's 65th character - the space, written to $699A as 255 - which no password in this profile uses.
the cursor     $0320 counts the characters entered; $0321/$0322 are the
keyboard row and column. THE CURSOR IS ONE INDEX OVER 65
CELLS, and row/column are read back out of it as
index // 13 and index % 13: Right/Left step it by +1/-1
and Up/Down by -13/+13, modulo 65. The axes are NOT
independent - a model that wraps row and column
separately picks the wrong cell for any move that crosses
a row boundary, and an early version of the generator did
exactly that and typed 'z' where '9' was meant. Measured,
every one of them: one Up from (0,0) gives (4,0) and one
Left gives (4,12); thirteen Rights from (4,0) and one
Down from it both land on (0,0); four Downs from (0,0)
return to it.
the typing     A types the character under the cursor and leaves the
cursor where it is. $699A (DataCrystal's 'Password
characters', in WRAM) holds each character typed as its
alphabet index, and that is what settles the model: four
Lefts from (0,0) then A writes $3D = 61 = 'z', index 61
being row 4, column 9 - where the flat index says four
Lefts land, and where independent axes would say (0,9)
= '9'. The generated script for 'Kraid's Lair, suitless'
writes exactly 09 x 12 then 14 x 12 at $699A, which is
the password '999999 999999 KKKKKK KKKKKK'.
Each value's entry script is generated from its password by
scripts/stages/metroid/password-entry.py, which carries that layout and
takes a shortest path along the ring for every character (a mix of the
one-cell and one-row steps is shorter than either alone), so the scripts
are mechanical and reproducible rather than hand-typed. Neither the
password nor the layout is a cheat: the game writes its own state through
its own password routine, which is ADR-0184 s3's rank 1 ('game code the
developers shipped') in its purest form.
THE PASSWORDS ARE THE SELECTOR, SO THEY TRAVEL VERBATIM. ADR-0184's
phrase for the obligation is 'the code travels with the art, verbatim and
with its address'. For an input selector there is no address, and the
string itself is what a later reader needs, so every value's title
carries it inside the note the sweep writes into notes[] - the profile
has no other way to put it there, and a title is the one field
record_navigation_sweep.py copies into that note. Each value also carries
the string as _password, its effect as _effect and its source as
_source, for a reader of this file.
ONE AREA CLAIM IS CONTRADICTED BY THE PUBLISHED TABLES, and the decode settles
it. '0Gz--- -m3e0G 00VvjS 3m00n?' is listed as Brinstar by one table and as
'ready for Kraid' by another; the password's own byte 8 decodes to Brinstar and
the ROM's $0074 wrote Brinstar when the recording was made, so the value is
kept as Brinstar on two independent votes. See
runs/f1417/metroid/RESULT.md for the per-value measurement.
THE RAM CHECK, AND WHAT IT PROVES. The address is DataCrystal's: '$0074 Current
level ($10 = Brinstar, $11 = Norfair, $12 = Kraid, $13 = Tourian, $14 =
Ridley)' for the four areas past Brinstar, and '$1D Engine mode (0 = game, 1 =
title/password)' for Brinstar itself. The expected byte is not typed beside the
password: scripts/stages/metroid/password-entry.py decodes the password with
the Metroid Password Format Guide's format and derives it, because the ROM's
level byte IS the password's own byte 8 - bits 0-2 the level (0 Brinstar, 1
Norfair, 2 Kraid, 3 Tourian as Norfair|Kraid, which is the guide's own rule, 4
Ridley) and bit 4 the $10 that every value DataCrystal documents carries. A
value whose byte 8 has bit 4 clear therefore lands on $01-$04 and not on
$11-$14, and the guide's bit 3 is called 'the reset bit ... there are 16
possible values, but only 5 valid ones' for the same reason: byte 8 is the
level byte, and everything outside $10-$14 is a combination the ROM's table
does not use.
Measured, not assumed: runs/f1417/metroid/probe/state/ holds one traced
recording per value with $0074 sampled every emulated second, and the byte is
written once - when the ROM accepts the password - and never changes again,
not on a door, not on a death, not on the title screen. It read
(byte 8 & 7) | (byte 8 & 0x10) in all eleven values that entered the game.
Brinstar is the exception, and it is a real one: level 0 and the value the
title screen rests on are both $00, so a $0074 check on a Brinstar value cannot
fail and is therefore not evidence - $00 is exactly what a session that never
left the password screen reads. Those two values check the engine mode
instead, which is the byte that separates a session in the game from one still
sitting on the selector screen.
Nothing in this profile is pinned, so no check carries ADR-0239 s4's caveat and
each one is the game's own byte. A check can only say which area the session
ended in - it cannot tell two values of the same area apart, which is what s4's
'new' count is for.
ONE VALUE WAS DROPPED, AND HOW IT WAS FOUND MATTERS. '4F---- ------ ------
------' is republished as a Brinstar code, but its 24 characters do not
reconcile the password format's checksum, so this ROM's password routine
refuses it: the recorded session sat on the password screen for its whole 120
seconds (engine mode $1D = 1 at every sample, $0074 = 0), never entered the
game, and still reported 143 'new' drawn keys - the characters and the cursor
the blind body typed onto the keyboard, which no baseline pack holds. ADR-0239
s4's gate reads 'new == 0 means did-not-warp'; this is the converse failing,
because a selector screen draws art of its own. A non-zero 'new' is therefore
not by itself proof of a warp: the check beside it is what says the session was
in the game. password-entry.py now refuses any password whose checksum does not
reconcile, so the same mistake cannot come back as a session that spends a
minute of capture budget being refused inside the emulator.
WHAT THIS SWEEP DOES NOT REACH. A password selects the area Samus starts
in; it does not select a room inside it, and the blind body below walks
the start room rather than clearing it. So:
- the area-to-area transition (the elevator and the map screen) is not
recorded by any session here. This is not ADR-0184's amendment in
action - nothing is pinned after the password is accepted, so a body
that cleared an area would record the transition. This body does not
clear one.
- every boss room (Kraid, Ridley), Mother Brain's room and the Metroid
corridors of Tourian are rung 3 work: a save state reached by search,
chain or movie, which a later measurement has to name (ADR-0239 s1).
- the endings and the escape sequence, for the same reason.
NO LIVES PIN, so ADR-0239 s3's inert control does not apply and is not
run. Metroid has no lives counter for a pin to hold: death returns Samus
to the entrance of the area she is in with 30 energy, and there is no
GAME OVER screen to foreclose. defaults.cheats is therefore absent and no
process in this sweep is launched with a cheat at all - the body below is
allowed to die (ADR-0184 s4).
THE REFERENCE PACK CANNOT BE SCORED (ADR-0239 s5.3). A real artist pack
for this ROM is on disk - the MEP v1.0.0 submission the pack manager
finds beside the ROM, whose pack.json targets this ROM's No-Intro SHA1 and
whose hires.txt declares <supportedRom>ecf39ec5a33e6a6f832f03e8ffc61c5d
53f4f90b, the whole-file SHA1 of this same dump, and whose md5 is
bab3f30abab8e52dc453f0b986a33f8b - but its 150250 <tile> rules name a tile
two or three hex digits, none of them the 16 bytes of a pattern) and this
ROM has no CHR to read an index through: byte 5 of its iNES header is 0,
so the pattern table is CHR RAM and is filled from PRG at run time. The
tool refuses rather than printing a figure, which is what s5.3 asks for,
and runs/f1417/metroid/RESULT.md records the refusal verbatim.

navigation.label: the title screen's CONTINUE option and the PASSWORD screen's keyboard
navigation.source: This ROM's own password screen, reached from the title screen with Start, then Select, then Start. The keyboard and the way it is read were measured off the ROM on 2026-09-26 and are written up in this profile's first _comment block and in scripts/stages/metroid/password-entry.py; the 64-character alphabet and the 24-character, four-group password are corroborated by the Metroid Password Format Guide (games.technoplaza.net/mpg/password.txt) and by metroidgen.py. Each password string and its published area are cited per value in _source below; the area and the RAM check are derived from the string by scripts/stages/metroid/password-entry.py and never typed beside it, and the decode is also what refuses a republished string the ROM would reject. ADR-0239 s1 rung 1: input, no cheat.

_defaultsComment: entry is a fallback: every value above names its own entry script, because the
password is what selects the place. It names brinstar-suitless, the shortest of
body is this set's own stage-1 route (scripts/stages/metroid/stage1-run.txt,
the route the metroid stage set already carries), repeated by
record_navigation_sweep.py until the 120 s budget is covered - exactly as
Contra's and Ninja Gaiden's profiles do. It is a blind body: it walks
right from the area's start room, shooting and jumping, and morphs into
the ball. It is not a route that clears anything, and it is the same body
in every area, so the sessions differ by where the password put Samus and
not by what the body does.
seconds is ADR-0239 s6's budget, and the entry scripts fit inside it: the
longest is tourian-suitless at 1864 frames (31.0 s), the shortest kraid at
1088 frames (18.1 s), so between 90 and 100 s of each session is the body.
